title: Simultaneous coefficient-system and normalized Roos comparison data
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Set $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and on the small pro-etale site set $B_n=(A_n)_s$ and $\widehat R_s=\lim_nB_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\mathscr S_s$ be the abelian category of strict $B_n$-module systems with quotient-linear transitions, with its ordinary unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $U_s$ for levelwise restriction to $\widehat R_s$-module towers and $\mathcal L_s=R\lim U_s$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Put $F_r=(h^r)^{-1}$ on module complexes with scalars transported through the canonical coefficient isomorphisms, and $G_r$ for its levelwise functor on systems [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Read the finite levels through $j_{r,M}:F_rM\to(h^r)^*M$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, of part (a) of the latter definition. Let $\Gamma_\bullet$ be restriction of scalars followed by exact sections levelwise, retaining all transitions [def-trf-coefficient-tower-operations, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

For any strict tower complex $V$ put $P_V=\prod_{n\geq1}V_n$, $s_V((v_n)_n)=(t_nv_{n+1})_n$, and
$$H(V)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_V)[-1],\qquad H(V)^i=P_V^{i-1}\oplus P_V^i,\qquad d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_V)a,da).$$
Use total right derived inverse limit and its normalized strict Roos comparison [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], whose strict augmentation is $z\mapsto(0,(\gamma_nz)_n)$.

Fix $r\geq1$. Put $T=\Gamma(s,-)$ with scalars restricted to $R$ through constant sections. There is a canonical natural identification of strict towers $U_sG_rM\cong F_r^{\operatorname{Tow}}U_sM$ for every unbounded complex $M$ of strict systems, using $j_{r,M_n}$ at each finite level and the coefficient identity $\pi_nc_{\widehat R}=c_nF_r(\pi_n)$; it retains the original quotient-linear transitions. Under it $T^{\operatorname{Tow}}U_sM=\Gamma_\bullet M$. Both $F_r$ and $T$ are additive exact functors with invertible canonical countable-product comparisons. Their projection formulas are evaluation of a product at $(V,h^rv)$ for $F_r$, and at $(s,\mathrm{id})$ for $T$; the module actions are the transported completed action and the constant $R$-action respectively. Countable products are exact in both ambient module categories [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact].

For $X=U_sM$ and $Y=U_sG_rM$ there are canonical natural chain isomorphisms
$$\kappa^F_X:F_rH(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(Y),\qquad \kappa^T_X:T H(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(T^{\operatorname{Tow}}X).$$
They apply the corresponding projection-characterized product comparison on both coordinates and have zero off-diagonal components. Write $\theta_X:\mathcal L_s[M]\xrightarrow{\sim}H(X)$ and $\eta_X:R\lim T^{\operatorname{Tow}}X\xrightarrow{\sim}H(T^{\operatorname{Tow}}X)$ for the fixed normalized total-limit identifications. Then
$$a_{r,[M]}=\theta_Y^{-1}\kappa^F_XF_r(\theta_X),\qquad \zeta_{[M]}=T(\theta_X^{-1})(\kappa^T_X)^{-1}\eta_X$$
are the restrictions to complexes of natural isomorphisms $a_r:F_r\mathcal L_s\cong\mathcal L_sG_r$ and $\zeta:R\lim\Gamma_\bullet\cong T\mathcal L_s$ on the entire ordinary unbounded derived system category. These same maps are obtained by applying the functors to the whole ordinary limit cone on tower resolutions; they are independent of those resolutions and preserve the strict augmentation with zero shifted coordinate [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. The signed-coordinate identification with that lemma is the natural chain isomorphism $J_V(b,a)=(a,-b)$ to $H'(V)^i=P_V^i\oplus P_V^{i-1}$ with $d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s_V)x-dy)$; it sends the augmentation to $((\gamma_nz)_n,0)$ and conjugates each diagonal comparison to the same product comparison on both summands. No constructibility, boundedness, normalization or completeness condition on $M$ or $\mathcal L_s[M]$ is imposed.

proof.text: At each finite coefficient level, use the pushforward composition and coefficient projection square to identify G followed by evaluation of U with evaluation of U followed by F. The component is identity on sections (HEq accounts for the transported coefficient action). Horizontal transition maps are the original section restrictions, by the unique specification of U, so module-sheaf extensionality assembles the level isomorphisms into a natural tower isomorphism. Apply this natural isomorphism degreewise to complexes. The finite tensor comparison is invertible by the existing finite comparison theorem.

Point sections are exact, and are evaluation followed by scalar restriction; both preserve the canonical products. Sectionwise exact products of pro-etale module sheaves give the source hypothesis, and Mathlib AB4 for ModuleCat gives the target hypothesis.

proof.text: For an arbitrary exact additive product-preserving functor Q, use the canonical additive Roos comparison. Its projections are Q applied to the original projections followed by the canonical product comparison. The product comparison is invertible, hence the whole chain comparison is invertible. The ordinary limit comparison is the termwise canonical preservesLimitNatIso, and is characterized by all its projections.

proof.text: The ordinary limit inclusion has coordinates (0, product of limit projections). Its comparison square follows by both biproduct projections and then all product projections. Descend the conjugated natural chain isomorphism through the ordinary derived localization. Cancel the fixed normalized theta in its representative equation to get compatibility with the derived-functor unit. Inverting the units on arbitrary K-injectives and using naturality proves the formula for every pair of resolutions; no termwise-injective restriction is imposed on those resolutions. Strict augmentations are preserved by the existing additive Roos augmentation formula.

proof.text: Use the normalized Roos isomorphism on the Grothendieck abelian tower category, with its unit as the specified natural transformation. The ordinary termwise limit is naturally the ordinary limit of complexes; the unit-normalized equality transfers along that isomorphism. On a K-injective the unit is invertible, so the ordinary inclusion is a quasi-isomorphism. This supplies one theta for both actual functors and one eta for scalar modules.

proof.text: The coordinate change J(b,a)=(a,-b) conjugates the strict Roos differential to d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s)x-dy). Prove this as a biproduct matrix identity from the original cone differential, using all four matrix entries. The same coordinate change carries a diagonal comparison to the same two product comparisons.

Package the coefficient identities, normalizations, comparison bundles and signed differential in the parametrized DataCore and specialize to the point system.
